beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Borrowed Credibility asks when a respected name starts doing the work of evidence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This book explains scientific trust through institutions that must ration scarce attention.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its opening thought experiment gives the same manuscript two different institutional pedigrees.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The words stay unchanged, but a famous laboratory can alter expectations.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Readers follow that gap without assuming either experts or outsiders are automatically right.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The recurring researcher, Elena Varga, is a composite created for this institutional journey.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Her manuscript lets the book separate attention, competence, evidence, and access to resources.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A laboratory's reputation can reasonably tell a reviewer where to begin looking.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It cannot replace checking the particular result once its evidence becomes available.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The proposed alternative connects claims with methods, data, code, and independent checks.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Those connections reveal what supports a claim, while leaving judgment open to challenge.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A paper can contain a reliable measurement and a much weaker interpretation.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Imagine a reviewer questioning that interpretation while retaining the underlying measurement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book's proposed infrastructure would make such distinctions easier to inspect and update.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It also asks who receives time, money, and credit for doing this work.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Better records alone cannot repair incentives that reward production while neglecting correction.
